newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DELY VALDES HITS TWO MORE FOR LEADERS PSG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DELY VALDES HITS TWO MORE FOR LEADERS PSG.

text.p: Julio Cesar Dely Valdes, whose Paris Saint-Germain future was in doubt only two weeks ago, scored twice as the French first division leaders remained six points clear with a 3-1 home win over Lille on Wednesday.

The Panama striker calmed home nerves in a 31,000 crowd with his first goal just after the half hour against PSG's bogey team, the last side to win a league match at the Parc des Princes back in April to dash their 1995-96 title hopes.
Brazil's Rai, calm and personified, played a significant role in PSG's two other goals.

He tapped a free kick to France midfielder Bruno N'Gotty who blasted a fine shot home four minutes later and selflessly laid the ball on for Dely Valdes in the 57th after breaking through with every chance of scoring himself.
Dely Valdes has scored five goals in four games for PSG to help them emerge from a lean spell with a place in the European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-finals and their title hopes intact.

Striker Patrick Collot, who scored the winner for Lille at the Parc in April, replied for the visitors with a 25-metre shot two minutes before the break that France goalkeeper Bernard Lama should have saved.
Lama said: "I'm annoyed because I shouldn't allow myself to concede goals like that, but it was the only mistake of the night.
"The great teams have the quality of being able to make the difference at any moment and that's what happened.
"Now we must keep up our momentum and take maximum points before the halfway stage."
PSG are away to Bordeaux and at home against arch-rivals Marseille in their next two difficult assignments.

Marseille, looking to consolidate on their fine home win over Monaco last week, managed only a 0-0 draw at Cannes and had Italian defender Ivan Franceschini sent off for the second time this season for a professional foul.
Lille coach Jean-Michel Cavalli, whose side lost 4-0 to PSG in a pre-season friendly, said: "I had feared worse. But we have nothing to be ashamed of. We didn't close up the game. We played."
French teenage hope Thierry Henry, who has been targetted by Real Madrid, scored his seventh goal of the season to send second placed Monaco on their way to a 2-0 home win over Strasbourg.
The second half substitute breathed some life into a lethargic Monaco side with a fine solo run to score in the 52nd minute.
Monaco's second was an own goal by defender Valerien Ismael near the end.
Champions Auxerre managed to stay in third place despite a disappointing 0-0 draw at Guingamp, the ground where they clinched their first championship last May.
Now nine points adrift of PSG, their coach Guy Roux said: "It was a good match and there were no goals simply because the defences played well, but I'm satisfied with the result."
Metz, watched by Kevin Keegan ahead of his Newcastle United side's visit next week for the first leg of the two sides UEFA Cup third round tie, are fourth after a 2-0 victory over Rennes.
It was a convincing win with goals by striker Stephane Adam and Senegal's Amara Traore.
Bordeaux, 3-1 up at halftime, survived a spirited final onslaught at Lens to win 4-3 and move into fifth place.

Lyon's former France international Christophe Cocard found his form at last and the net twice in his side's 3-1 home win over Nice, whose defender Bruno Calegari was sent off for a foul on the striker midway through the second half.

Nantes, the 1995 champions who did not win in their first 10 matches, extended their unbeaten run to 10 games with a 2-0 home win over Nancy on Tuesday. Now 10th, they climbed into the top half of the standings for the first time this season.
